cross_cutting: Calibration: the 0.8 GiB overhead plus a desktop sum under-predicted the only measured offload run by 98 MiB (Qwen3.6: 15,092 predicted, 15,190 measured, llamacpp/benchmarking.md:353). Every plan that sits within 100 MiB of the 15,341 floor fails before anything else is wrong: Gemma (+30), Bolt (+54), MoVA (+95) and Lightning (+102). Add +100 MiB to every offload prediction until a second model is measured.

Large-batch staging (estimate from how ggml_backend_sched allocates copies of host weights in the compute buffer): the measured 0.72 GiB on Qwen3.6 hid a 432 MiB per-block expert copy under its 485 MiB logits buffer. Models whose per-block host experts exceed their logits buffer pay the difference: Coder-Next (712 vs 297 MiB), Lightning (685 vs 256) and Bolt (up to 639 vs 256). The worst-case compute buffer is reserved at load, so the 'CUDA0 compute buffer size' log line checks this before the first prompt. Record it for every model.

Policy for every offloaded plan: start with the MoE cache 256-384 MiB below the plan, read the load log and the nvidia-smi peak after the longest probe, then raise --moe-cache-mib in 256 MiB steps while at least 500 MiB stays free. A too-small margin aborts mid-prefill (#31974). --fit does not trim once -ngl and --n-cpu-moe are set.

Container caps with -lm none must count pinned experts + token_embd + --cache-ram + context checkpoints (SWA or recurrent state x n_ctx_checkpoints) + about 2 GiB of process. The worst cases of Coder-Next (35.1 > 35g) and Bolt (25.9 vs 26g) break or touch the cap. Bound them with -ctxcp. Always set --memory equal to --memory-swap, because heavy does not reach containers.
